questions.question: Define density, give its formula and two units, and explain why a small and a large piece of the same metal have the same density.
questions.expected_answer: Density is the mass per unit volume of a substance: density = mass ÷ volume (ρ = m/V). Units: g/cm³ or kg/m³ (1 g/cm³ = 1 000 kg/m³). A larger piece has more mass but also proportionally more volume, so the ratio of mass to volume is the same; density is a property of the substance, not the size of the object.

questions.question: A stone has a mass of 54 g. Water in a measuring cylinder rises from 40 mL to 60 mL when it is submerged. Calculate its density, and calculate the mass of 1 litre of cooking oil of density 0.92 g/cm³.
questions.expected_answer: Volume of stone = 60 − 40 = 20 mL = 20 cm³. Density = m ÷ V = 54 g ÷ 20 cm³ = 2.7 g/cm³. Oil: volume 1 L = 1 000 cm³; mass = density × volume = 0.92 g/cm³ × 1 000 cm³ = 920 g.

questions.question: Use the particle model to explain why steam is much less dense than liquid water and why ice floats. State the rule for floating and explain why a steel ship floats though steel sinks.
questions.expected_answer: In steam the same water particles are far apart with large empty spaces, about 1 700 times the volume of the liquid, so the same mass occupies much more volume and the density is much lower. When water freezes, the molecules lock into an open six-sided arrangement that takes up about 9% more volume than the liquid, so ice (0.92 g/cm³) is less dense than water (1.00 g/cm³) and floats. Rule: an object floats if its average density is less than that of the fluid and sinks if it is greater. A ship's hull encloses a large volume of air, so its total mass divided by its total volume is less than the density of water, even though steel itself is about 7.9 g/cm³.
